meta.description: Orchestrates the untargeted LC-MS metabolomics pipeline end-to-end (xcms 4.x feature extraction, QC/drift/normalization, confidence-stratified annotation, permutation-validated statistics, background-aware pathway mapping), naming what each stage decides and where it silently fails.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/p-values/effect sizes anywhere; all reported numbers came from real xcms/pmp/ropls output on real faahKO/MTBLS79 data or the bundled synthetic example, both labeled correctly.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-only mouse/serum metabolomics pipeline; no individual diagnostic or prescriptive claims, no medical-disclaimer-requiring content.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled statistical fallacy found (BH FDR, permutation-validated OPLS-DA, background-aware ORA are all correctly specified in principle); the mode-lock and MSI-gate enforcement gaps (Inputs 4, 6) are completeness/documentation gaps, not incorrect methodology.

code_usability.detail: The one bundled, self-contained runnable file (examples/metabolomics_workflow.R) executed cleanly end-to-end and recovered 20/20 planted hits. A real crash was found (Input 2) when chaining the Stage2->Stage4 SKILL.md code snippets on real multi-batch data, but this is scored hard in code executability and flagged as P1 recommendations rather than vetoed, consistent with sibling component-Skill audits' treatment of similar reproducible snippet bugs.

functional_suitability.note: Thorough 5-stage decision table and pipeline-flow diagram, but two real correctness defects were found in the documented Stage1->Stage2 and Stage2->Stage4 code snippets (see Inputs 1-2).

reliability.note: Common Errors table is useful but omits both hand-off bugs found by execution; QC Checkpoints table gives good refresh-routing for component-level failures.

performance_context.note: Concise (230 lines), defers detail to component Skills well, good token economy.

agent_usability.note: Clear trigger phrasing, explicit stage ownership table; consistency suffers slightly where prose commitments have no matching code (Inputs 4, 6).

human_usability.note: Natural example prompts, good discoverability; forgiveness path (Refresh -> where) is well structured.

security.note: No credential exposure, injection vectors, or destructive operations anywhere in the orchestration code.

maintainability.note: Modular hand-off to 8 component Skills, but the one bundled example never exercises the real multi-package seams (Stage 1/3/5 fully commented out) -- exactly where both real bugs found here live.

agent_specific.note: Strong trigger precision and composability (workflow:true, depends_on frontmatter); no escape-hatch/idempotency handling shown for a broken hand-off (Input 2's crash has no recovery guidance).

inputs.label: Stage1->Stage2 xcms-to-pmp orientation hand-off, real faahKO feature table
inputs.note: SKILL.md's `fm <- t(feat)` inverts the orientation its own comment claims; pmp's check_peak_matrix silently auto-corrects via classes-length matching, so real execution succeeds but only by luck of a downstream defensive check, not by the documented code being correct.

assertions.text: Workflow's Stage1->Stage2 code produces the pmp orientation its own comment claims
assertions.note: t(feat) on real 574x12 xcms output produces 12x574 (samples-in-rows), the opposite of the comment's claim.

assertions.text: Real xcms output can be fed through the documented transform without crashing
assertions.note: filter_peaks_by_fraction ran without error on both the transposed and untransposed matrix, returning the same 573x12 result via pmp's own auto-detection.

assertions.text: SKILL.md flags the orientation-sensitivity risk it silently depends on
assertions.note: No mention anywhere that correctness relies on pmp's classes-length auto-detection rather than the documented transpose being correct.

assertions.text: No security/injection issues in the hand-off code
assertions.note: Plain matrix transpose and CSV read; no unsafe operations.

inputs.label: Real Stage2->Stage4 chain on MTBLS79 (cow/sheep serum, 8 batches, 38 QCs)
inputs.note: Running the workflow's documented pmp Stage-2 chain then `t(normalized)[study_samples,]` into opls() on real biological data crashed with 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed'. Root cause: 5 of 8 real batches have only 4 QC injections (< the workflow's own minQC=5 default), triggering QCRSC's known silent all-NA-per-batch bug (already flagged in the normalization-qc audit); the result is 55.95% NA cells fed straight into opls() because the workflow's Stage 4 code snippet never calls the imputation step it only names in a comment.

assertions.text: Documented Stage2->Stage4 code chain runs end-to-end on real multi-batch biological data
assertions.note: opls() threw 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed'.

assertions.text: Stage 2 output's missingness is imputed before entering Stage 4 as the pipeline's own text states
assertions.note: No imputation call exists between pqn_normalisation and opls() in the SKILL.md code; imputation is named only in a trailing comment.

assertions.text: Feature/sample orientation is correct at the Stage2->Stage4 boundary
assertions.note: t(normalized)[study_samples,] correctly produced 134 samples x 2433 features for opls().

assertions.text: A failure at this hand-off surfaces an actionable, pipeline-aware message

The component Skill (metabolite-annotation) does emit a usable per-feature level in its own real output, so the data needed exists -- the orchestrator just never shows the filter step.

key_strengths: The bundled reference example (examples/metabolomics_workflow.R) is real, runs cleanly end-to-end, and correctly recovers all 20 planted true-effect features from synthetic Stage 2+4 data.
The five-stage QC-checkpoint table and 'Refresh (fail) -> where' routing give a genuinely useful failure-triage map back to the right component Skill.
The MS-DIAL alternate front-end claim (enter at Stage 2) is real: both Skills independently converge on the same features-in-rows/samples-in-columns table shape.
No credential, injection, or destructive-operation exposure anywhere in the orchestration code.
When pushed to shortcut confidence-level tagging, the Skill's own stated principles are strong enough to make an agent hold the line without just refusing outright.

recommendations.title: Stage2->Stage4 hand-off crashes on real multi-batch data: imputation is a comment, not code
recommendations.problem: The documented `t(normalized)[study_samples,]` -> opls() call throws 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed' on real MTBLS79 data (55.95% NA cells), because QCRSC's known silent all-NA behavior on thin-QC batches (already flagged in the normalization-qc audit) reaches opls() unimputed.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's Stage 2 code block names imputation only in a trailing comment ('Impute only the sparse residual holes... see normalization-qc') instead of calling it, so the orchestrator's own worked Stage 4 example receives an unimputed matrix.
recommendations.fix: Insert an explicit imputation call (impute.QRILC/missForest per mechanism) between pqn_normalisation and opls() in the Stage 4 code block, and add 'no missing values remain before OPLS-DA' to a QC checkpoint.

recommendations.title: Stage1->Stage2 orientation comment contradicts its own code
recommendations.problem: `fm <- t(feat)` is captioned 'features in ROWS, samples in COLUMNS (pmp convention)' but featureValues() output is already features-in-rows, so the transpose inverts it; correctness only survives because pmp's check_peak_matrix silently auto-detects and re-transposes via the classes-length match.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippet appears to assume a samples-in-rows input without re-checking against the featureValues() convention documented earlier in the same file.
recommendations.fix: Remove the erroneous transpose (feed `feat` directly to pmp) or correct the comment to state the true post-transpose orientation, and add a `stopifnot` dimension check so a future regression is caught rather than silently masked.

recommendations.title: Two of the three governing commitments have no enforcing code anywhere
recommendations.problem: The ionization-mode lock and the MSI-confidence gate before ORA are stated as prose/QC-checkpoint rows but never appear as code in SKILL.md or the bundled example; only the block-randomization commitment is actually demonstrated in runnable code.
recommendations.root_cause: The orchestrator is written as a narrative sequencer over component Skills rather than as a checkable hand-off contract at each Skill boundary.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal snippet at Stage 3->5 that filters annotated compounds to MSI Level 1-2 before building `identified_compounds`, and thread a `mode` column through the feature table with a check before Stage 3/5 that all rows share one ionization mode.

recommendations.title: The bundled example never exercises the seams it claims to unify
recommendations.problem: examples/metabolomics_workflow.R runs cleanly but only synthesizes Stage 2 and Stage 4 in base R; Stage 1, 3, and 5 -- where both real bugs above live -- are fully commented out, so the one runnable artifact never tests the actual multi-package hand-offs.
recommendations.root_cause: Stage 1/3/5 need real instrument files, SIRIUS-class tools, or MetaboAnalystR's network dependency, which are hard to bundle in a self-contained example.
recommendations.fix: Ship a second, smaller example chaining real (or cached) Stage 1 output through Stage 2's real pmp calls into a real Stage 4 opls() call on a tiny toy dataset, so regressions like the two found here are caught automatically.
